newsitem.title: USA: Teen-ager turns himself in on baby-death charge.
newsitem.headline: Teen-ager turns himself in on baby-death charge.

text.p: An 18-year-old college student was being held in state prison after surrendering to authorities here Thursday on charges he helped his girlfriend murder her newborn son.
A glum-looking Brian Peterson, accompanied by his lawyer and mother, fought through a crush of media and turned himself over to the FBI on a fugitive warrant.
He was taken to police in Newark, Del., where he was booked on first-degree murder charges, then to Gander Hill prison in Wilmington for an arraignment hearing.
Peterson was being held without bail in the Gander Hill infirmary for mental and physical evaluation. He was also to be subjected to blood tests to help determine whether he fathered the dead child.
Peterson's girlfriend, Amy Grossberg, surrendered Monday and was charged in the infant's death.
Both could face the death penalty if convicted.
Peterson's attorney, Joseph Hurley, told reporters Peterson broke down crying after entering FBI headquarters. "He's crying upstairs," Hurley said.
He later described a tearful separation between Peterson and his mother. "Everybody's crying, then he would say it's going to be ok ... he'e trying to comfort her, she's trying to comfort him."

Police say Peterson and Grossberg, 18, murdered the baby boy after Grossberg gave birth last week in a motel room in Delaware. They are accused of hitting the baby in the head and stuffing him into a plastic bag, which they dumped in a trash can before dawn last Tuesday.

The body was found the next day. An autopsy showed the baby died of severe skull fractures. The motel was just a few miles from the University of Delaware where Grossberg is a freshman. Peterson, who allegedly helped with the baby's delivery, is a freshman at Gettysburg College in Pennsylvania.
Hurley said Peterson "is not a murderer who deserves to die."

"He didn't commit murder. He commited a crime of bad judgment because no two teenagers that have no medical training should be alone in a motel when a baby is being delivered," Hurley told Fox television.

Hurley also said the death penalty was unwarranted in the case. "I think it's lamentable at this stage that anybody would say that you kill two kids who took the life of a kid, even if you assume he, they, took the life of a kid."
